onboarding.handle: Your public address in Porukam — like an @name in a messenger. Counterparties find you by it and it opens your reputation card. Latin letters, digits, dot and underscore.
onboarding.name: The name the other party sees in the contract and on your card. First name only or first and last — the way you introduce yourself at work.

contractNew.title: A short contract name for the list — e.g. “Kitchen renovation” or “Logo for a café”. Leave empty and the description is used.
contractNew.workDescription: What exactly must be done: scope, result, what counts as finished. The more specific, the easier acceptance is and the fewer disputes.
contractNew.locationType: Where the work happens: at the customer’s, the contractor’s, remotely or at an address. Access and handover terms depend on it.
contractNew.locationAddress: Work site address — street, building, floor and unit if needed. Visible only to the parties.
contractNew.termType: How the term is counted: by start and end dates, or by a number of days from signing.
contractNew.start: The date the contractor starts the work.
contractNew.end: The date by which the work must be fully delivered.
contractNew.durationDays: How many calendar days the work takes, counted from the signing date.
contractNew.priceType: A fixed price for the whole scope, or payment per stage/unit. Stages are handier for complex work.
contractNew.currency: The currency of every amount in the contract. One per contract — cannot be changed after signing.
contractNew.warrantyDays: How many days after acceptance the contractor is responsible for defects. 0 — no warranty.
contractNew.acceptanceHours: How many hours the customer has to check a delivered stage. No answer in time — the stage is accepted automatically.
contractNew.paymentMethod: How the parties settle: bank transfer, cash, other. The platform never holds or moves money — it only records the agreement and the facts.
contractNew.paymentOrder: When each stage is paid: before it starts (prepayment) or after the customer accepts it (postpayment). Applies to every stage of the contract.
contractNew.subcontract: Whether the contractor may bring in helpers or other contractors for part of the work.
contractNew.premisesAccess: Whether the contractor needs access to the customer’s premises and on what terms (hours, keys, presence).
contractNew.portfolioConsent: Whether the customer allows showing the result in the contractor’s portfolio after acceptance.
contractNew.stages: Split the work into stages: each is delivered and accepted separately, and the stage amounts add up to the contract price. One stage is enough for a small job.
contractNew.stageTitle: What is delivered at this stage — e.g. “Draft layout” or “Installation”.
contractNew.stageAmount: The price of this stage only. All stages together must equal the contract price.
contractNew.stageDeadline: The date by which the stage must be delivered to the customer for review.
contractNew.counterparty: Who the other party is: search by @handle or pick from saved contacts. This exact person receives the invitation.

sale.what: What is being sold — the item name as you would describe it to a buyer: “iPhone 13 128 GB”, “Trek FX 2 bicycle”.
sale.description: Condition, what’s included, specifics — everything the buyer should know before the deal.
sale.condition: New, like new, used with wear — an honest condition description protects both sides in a dispute.
sale.defects: Known defects and flaws. If nothing is listed, the buyer may expect there are none.
sale.completeness: What comes with it: box, charger, documents, accessories.
sale.identifiers: Serial number, IMEI, VIN etc. — they confirm that exactly this item was handed over.
sale.householdPlot: Tick if you sell produce from your own household plot — it affects the tax regime.
sale.price: The full price of the item. Paid delivery, if any, is set separately below.
sale.deliveryType: How the item is handed over: pickup, courier, post or a carrier.
sale.address: Handover or delivery address. Visible only to the parties.
sale.deliveryPayer: Who pays for delivery — the seller or the buyer.
sale.tracking: Whether a tracking number is required. It makes proving dispatch and receipt easier.
sale.deliveryTerm: Handover term: a specific date or a number of days after payment.
sale.deliveryDate: The date by which the item must be handed to the buyer.
sale.deliveryDays: How many days for handover, counted from the payment date.
sale.inspectionHours: How many hours the buyer has to inspect the item after receipt before the deal counts as closed.

settings.displayName: The name counterparties see next to your handle. Write it the way your clients know you.
settings.city: A free-text caption for towns not yet in our directory — shown on your card, but it does not affect search. Set your searchable work area below.
settings.handle: Your public address — people find you by it and open your reputation card. From 3 to 20 characters: Latin letters, digits, underscore.
settings.avatar: Counterparties see your profile photo in contracts, chats and on your card. A real face invites a deal more than a picture does.
settings.country: The country whose law governs your contracts (jurisdiction). It has nothing to do with your address or where you look for work, and currencies and taxes don't depend on it.
settings.phone: The number lets people who already have it find you by phone. It is not published in your profile.

notif.deals: Contract invitations, proposed revisions, signing, stage acceptance — everything about how deals progress.
notif.chats: New messages in contract chats and in enquiries.
notif.deadlines: Deadline reminders: the acceptance window is running out, a stage delivery date is coming up.
notif.disputes: A dispute opened, replies from the parties and decisions on the dispute.

stage.totalCost: Total cost of the work. Enter it and the amount is split evenly across stages — you can then adjust each stage by hand.
stage.title: What is delivered at this stage — “Draft layout”, “Installation”, “First batch”. Both sides see the name and it goes into the contract.
stage.amount: What this particular stage costs. The stage amounts must add up to the contract price, otherwise the contract cannot be frozen.
stage.duration: How many days the stage takes. Counted from the start of the stage, not from the signing of the contract.
stage.checklist: Acceptance criteria: the points the customer checks the stage against. Keep them measurable — “two layout revisions”, “walls with no streaks”: there is little left to argue about.
stage.evidence: A point marked “evidence required” expects an attached photo or file: without one a warning appears when the stage is submitted, but submission is not blocked. Evidence stays in the contract file and helps in a dispute.

materials.name: A material from the catalogue — that way the name and units match on both sides. Not listed? Pick “other” and type your own.
materials.customName: The name of the material in your own words, if the catalogue has no match.
materials.quantity: How much is needed — a number, in the units you selected.
materials.unit: The unit the quantity is measured in: pieces, metres, kilograms, litres.
materials.delivery: How many days the material takes to arrive. Helps to see whether the stage deadline is realistic.
materials.deliveryBase: The event the delivery time is counted from: contract signing, prepayment or stage start. That keeps the deadline independent of a calendar date.
materials.suppliedBy: Who buys and brings the material — the customer or the contractor. Disagreement here is a common cause of downtime.
materials.price: The price of one unit in the contract currency. For a contractor-supplied material it is required and above zero; a customer-supplied material may be free.

group.handle: The public address of the group — like @name in a messenger. It opens the group page and is what people link to.
group.name: What the group is called for people. Visible to anyone who opens its page.
group.sphere: The group’s main field of activity. People find it by that field in search, and it helps match members.
group.geo: The group’s reach: the whole world, one country or a single city. It decides who sees the group in search.
group.country: The country of reach. Required if the reach is “country” or “city”.
group.city: The main city of reach. Required when the reach is “city”.
group.description: What the group is about and who you are waiting for: what you do, what the rules are, how you help members.
group.visibility: An open group is visible to everyone and shows up in search; a closed one — only to members and by a direct link.
group.joinPolicy: How people get in: freely with a button, or by request approved by the owner.
group.links: Links to the group elsewhere — a site, a channel, a chat. Up to 10, shown on the group page.
group.logo: The group’s logo image: shown in search, on the card and next to the name. A square image looks best.

portfolio.title: What to call this work — “Kitchen in a panel house”, “One-page site for a coffee shop”.
portfolio.sphere: The field this work belongs to. People looking for something similar find your work by it.
portfolio.startedAt: When you took the work on. Optional, but together with the completion date it shows how long it took.
portfolio.completedAt: When the work was finished. Required: portfolio entries are ordered by this date.
portfolio.city: The city where the work was done. Helps customers nearby pick a contractor close to them.
portfolio.description: What was done, what difficulties you handled, how it turned out. No length limit.
portfolio.photos: Up to 5 photos of the work. The first one is the cover in the list; you can change the cover at any time.

revision.item: Which contract term you propose to change. The list holds the fields of this contract; “other” is free text.
revision.before: The current value from the contract. It is filled in automatically and cannot be edited — so both sides see the same thing.
revision.after: The new value of the term. The other side will accept or reject it; until they agree, the contract stays as it is.
revision.comment: Why the revision is needed. The other side sees the comment — a short explanation speeds up agreement.

signing.declineComment: What exactly did not suit you and what to fix. The other side sees this text and it stays in the contract history.
